analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations (Vogel), 20 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities liquidated on 11/19: S&P -202bps to 7,175 after a roughly 400bp intraday fade (reversing 3.3% intraday), NDX -221bps to 26,517, R2K -202bps to 2,659, Dow -219bps to 49,097. Only 38 S&P constituents advanced against 464 decliners. Desk (Privorotsky) calls it a pretty violent liquidation despite catalysts that were meant to be supportive.

Privorotsky cites new BIS chip export rules effective Nov 19 that restrict direct chip sales to China and advanced compute accessed remotely by Chinese entities through overseas data centers. He sees the immediate issue as uncertainty over who can access what under which licensing regime, which could freeze incremental investment decisions. He says this partly explains the weak Asian data center trade.

Privorotsky lists four drivers of lower multiples: cost of capital (made harder by a change of leadership at NVDA), data center restrictions, oversupply and efficiency gains in inference, and lack of revenue to support capex.

Defensive bid failed: utilities and staples sold off with everything else despite lower Treasury yields. They outperformed only in relative terms. Privorotsky says a rolling rotation increasingly looks like outright equity liquidation.

Negative gamma into expiry likely amplified the move. The US desk estimates dealers are near maximum short vega going into regular expiry on 11/20, and says some of those options need to unwind for the market to settle.

Financial conditions tightened very quickly. Privorotsky cites Waller's 50bp comments and mostly hawkish Fed speakers this week, draws parallels to Nov/Dec 2018, and says the Fed risks overtightening into a market already under stress. 2yr breakevens have collapsed toward lows while 2yr real yields are near relative highs.

Privorotsky prefers receiving rates and owning duration, which he says is misaligned with what equity internals show. He expects the market to pivot when central banks pivot, and sees gold as a coincident indicator reacting to real rates and financial conditions.

Privorotsky says depth of pessimism and one-sided de-grossing suggest the market may be nearing a tactical local low, but there are few catalysts ahead: PCE next Wednesday, NFP, the December FOMC, with November CPI the next major anchor.

Asia flows: GS desk investors were net sellers of $2bn for the week. China -$1.9bn, Hong Kong -$600mn, Korea -$441mn. Japan +$575mn and Taiwan +$394mn net bought. Info Tech was -$1.3bn of selling and every sector except Property was net sold.

Prime book data: Asia-focused fundamental L/S managers are down 1.6% MTD in November (MXAP -5.6%) and up 12.4% YTD on a weighted basis. Asian Info Tech/AI long sales exceeded short sales 2.4 to 1. Net allocation to Taiwan is back to February levels and to Korea to early-January levels.

China A-shares fell for a second week: SHCOMP -1.56% WTD, ChiNext -5.47%. Turnover hit 1.3bn Rmb Thursday, the lowest since July 2025. AI exporters (Innolight -12.4%) fell while domestic AI hardware and semi equipment held up. NT-favored ETFs took 97bn Rmb of inflows over 4 sessions, about 489bn Rmb since mid-October.

India: Nifty +1.5% this week. FIIs bought $10.8bn in November, the highest ever month-to-date inflow, and FII index shorts fell from a $5bn peak to $1.3bn. DIIs sold $6.2bn. INR is below 93.5/$ versus above 96 in October. GS upgraded India to overweight with a Nifty target of 28,500 by end-2027.

Korea: KOSPI is barely holding 5,000. GS GIR says the KOSPI semiconductor index is down more than 54% from its June peak, which discounts roughly a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings. GS cut its KOSPI target to 7,500 from 9,000. Korea ex-memory trades at about 6.9x NTM P/E.

Taiwan fell 17.5% WoW. Foreigners sold $6bn on the week, bringing TWSE net selling to $99bn YTD, including $75bn in TSMC. Domestic funds ended a 24-day net buying streak. Retail margin balances remain elevated, especially in TPEx, which the desk flags as a risk of further forced selling.

Japan: Nikkei -6.9% and TPX -6% on the week. GS Japan AI baskets fell 15-16%. Kioxia retail margin balance is at YTD highs (52.6mn shares on 11/18) while average cost per share has fallen, which suggests retail averaging down. The desk flags possible margin calls early next week. Japan-focused managers are -2% MTD, 7.6% YTD.

GS GIR 2027 Asia outlook: MXAPJ target 960, implying 19% USD price return on 26% earnings growth. Raise China H and India to overweight, cut Taiwan and China A to market weight, keep Korea and Japan overweight, underweight Australia and parts of ASEAN. Raise utilities to market weight and cut property to underweight.

US derivatives: VIX +1665bps to 28.65 and spot VIX traded more than 4 vol points over UX1, the most inverted term structure since April 2025. The 11/20 straddle priced a 1.43% move. Flows were put and put-spread buying, with 20k VIX Dec put trees bought, and no appetite to fade the move.

US tape and liquidity: MOC imbalance was $5.6bn to buy. S&P top-of-book averaged only $4mm. Volume was 20.873bn shares versus a YTD average of 18.566bn. Asset managers and hedge funds net sold macro products and net bought pockets of consumer and financials.

Single-stock moves: PANW +6% on earnings, INTC +2%, ESTC -8% and INTU -13% after hours on earnings. The desk notes an AMD short report was cited by some as a sentiment drag and mentions a record-size IPO that debuted with robust demand.

sector_views.rationale: GS GIR raised Asia utilities to market weight on structural power-demand tailwinds. In the US, utilities sold off with the market on 11/19 despite lower yields.
GS GIR remains overweight Asia tech hardware, though it cut Taiwan and China A to market weight to balance AI tech exposure.
GS GIR is overweight India banks, citing rate hikes, low valuations and light positioning, and Asia banks ex-Australia.
GS GIR cut Asia property to underweight.

INTU -13% and ESTC -8% after hours on earnings reaction on 11/19 (move reported in the desk note, no EPS or revenue figures given).
Upcoming: Japan desk lists NVDA earnings as a key catalyst for the coming week.

Oil rose slightly while equities and gold liquidated.
Gold liquidated alongside equities, which Privorotsky reads as a reaction to real rates and financial conditions.

trade_ideas.rationale: Privorotsky says it is the one trade misaligned with what equity internals have been signaling, and that he still finds it attractive.

trade_ideas.description: Long Asia ex-memory Korea China-play sectors (entertainment, cosmetics, tourism, duty free)
trade_ideas.rationale: Investors are revisiting laggards after China pledged most-favored-nation treatment to South Korea, and positioning in these non-AI sectors is light.
GS GIR cites mid-teen earnings growth, strong domestic demand and decade-low foreign positioning.

risk_factors: Further forced selling or margin calls in Japan and Taiwan from elevated retail margin balances.
Negative gamma and dealer short vega into expiry could amplify moves.
Poor liquidity: S&P top of book averaged only $4mm.
The Fed overtightening into a stressed market, with Nov/Dec 2018 parallels.
Further US chip export restrictions and licensing uncertainty freezing AI investment.
Limited catalysts until PCE, NFP and the December FOMC.

vol_and_positioning: VIX +1665bps to 28.65, with spot VIX more than 4 vol points above UX1, the most inverted term structure since April 2025.
SPX and NDX fixed-strike vols were bid, with gamma tenors closing just under +1 vol. The straddle for 11/20 priced a 1.43% move.
Flows were put and put-spread buying. A VIX Dec put tree was bought 20k times as a vol-lower trade. No appetite to fade the move.
The desk estimates dealers are near maximum short vega going into regular expiry on 11/20 and says some of those options need to unwind for stability.
Negative gamma into expiry likely amplified the 11/19 move.
Hedge funds de-grossed in Asia Info Tech/AI with long sales exceeding short sales 2.4 to 1. Taiwan and Korea net allocation reverted to February and early-January levels.
Japan: Kioxia retail margin balance at YTD highs and falling average cost points to retail averaging down, with margin call risk flagged for early next week.
Taiwan retail margin balances remain elevated relative to market cap, near July rally highs in TPEx.
India: FII index futures net short $1.3bn, down from a $5bn peak.
Privorotsky says the depth of pessimism and one-sided de-grossing suggest a tactical local low may be near.
geopolitical: New BIS export rules effective November 19, directed by Treasury and the NSC, tighten restrictions on chip sales to China and on remote access to advanced compute by Chinese entities through overseas data centers, with overlap with the proposed RASA legislation.
APEC meeting in Shenzhen: Trump and Xi met for the third time this year, and the first trilateral Trump, Xi and Putin meeting was held.
China pledged most-favored-nation treatment to South Korea in movies and games, which the desk says supports Korea's China-play sectors.

tension_points.bull_case: Depth of pessimism and one-sided de-grossing suggest the market may be approaching a tactical local low, and some of the forced funding or liquidation may not repeat.
tension_points.bear_case: Breaking this many charts across this many assets is not a bull market tape, financial conditions tightened sharply, and the defensive bid failed, so liquidation may continue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hawkish recalibration from the Fed, with November CPI named as the next event that could force it, would extend the stress.

tension_points.bull_case: KOSPI semiconductor index is down more than 54% from its June peak, discounting roughly a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings, and FY3 P/B near 0.7x is historically associated with cycle troughs.
tension_points.bear_case: Flow support is lacking, sentiment in AI and large cap tech has not recovered, and uncertainty remains over AI capex sustainability and geopolitical headwinds.
